items.stem: Before matching an ERP export, what check best confirms the file is complete?

options.text: Compare the export's control total and row count to the source system
options.rationale: Correct: reconciling control totals and counts detects truncated or partial exports.

options.text: Open the file and read the first ten rows
options.rationale: Reading a few rows does not confirm the whole file arrived.

options.text: Trust the file because it downloaded without an error
options.rationale: A clean download can still be incomplete or filtered.
Deleting rows corrupts the reconciliation and hides real items.

items.explanation: Correct: reconciling control totals and counts detects truncated or partial exports.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep ChatGPT-assisted variance analysis trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Trace each AI explanation back to the underlying source rows
options.rationale: Correct: verification against source keeps conclusions grounded.

options.text: Keep the AI output as a draft that a preparer confirms
options.rationale: Correct: treating output as a draft preserves human accountability.

options.text: Post AI conclusions straight into the final report
options.rationale: Unverified conclusions can carry errors into the report.

options.text: Hide the prompt so the method cannot be reviewed

items.explanation: Correct: verification against source keeps conclusions grounded.

items.stem: Why parameterise the source file path in a Power Query reconciliation?

options.text: So the query refreshes cleanly against next period's file
options.rationale: Correct: a parameter lets the same query run each period without edits.

options.text: Because it removes the need to validate inputs
options.rationale: Validation is still required regardless of parameters.

options.text: Because it deletes old data automatically
